items.question: How must this teaching be guarded in the world of mortals?
premises: The teaching must be concealed
Concealment requires deliberate effort
The mortal world contains the lowest of men
items.inference: Therefore the teaching should be carefully hidden among unworthy people in the mortal world.
items.plain_english: It must be carefully concealed in the mortal world among the lowest of men.

items.question: To whom may this teaching rightly be given after prior accomplishment?
premises: The teaching is to be given
The recipient should be previously accomplished
The recipient must be tested for one year
items.inference: Therefore the teaching may be given only to a previously accomplished person tested for one year.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is already accomplished and has been tested for one year.

items.question: Which chapter concludes in the section emerged from Candradvīpa?
premises: The text refers to a section emerged from Candradvīpa
A chapter is being identified
The chapter is the fifth
items.inference: Therefore this marks the conclusion of the fifth chapter in the Candradvīpa section.
items.plain_english: Thus ends the fifth chapter in the section that emerged from Candradvīpa.

items.question: By whose grace has the determination of the Kaula teaching been known?
premises: The speaker addresses the lord of Kaulas
Knowledge arose by that lord's grace
The Kaula determination is now known
items.inference: Therefore the speaker has come to know the Kaula determination through the lord's grace.
items.plain_english: O Lord of the Kaulas, by your grace I have come to know the determination of the Kaula teaching.

items.question: What is the soul that is declared, and what is its true nature?
premises: A soul has been declared in the teaching
Its identity is questioned
Its essential nature is also questioned
items.inference: Therefore clarification is sought about both the identity and nature of the soul.
items.plain_english: Who is that soul that has been declared, and what is the nature of the soul?

items.question: Into what does the soul dissolve, and what full explanation is requested?
premises: The soul's dissolution is questioned
The locus of dissolution is unknown
A complete explanation is requested
items.inference: Therefore the teacher is asked to explain fully where the soul dissolves.
items.plain_english: And into what does it dissolve? Tell me all of that.

items.question: What supreme qualities define the true nature of that soul?
premises: The soul is identified as supreme
The soul is partless and eternal
The soul is free from disease and stain
items.inference: Therefore the soul's true nature is supremely pure, partless, and eternal.
items.plain_english: He is supreme, partless, eternal, free from disease, and stainless.

items.question: How is the supreme soul identified as haṃsa and as the individual of power?
premises: The soul is described as supreme
That same soul is identified as haṃsa
That soul is also called the individual of power
items.inference: Therefore the supreme soul is equated with haṃsa, the individual constituted by power.
uncertainties: The exact doctrinal sense of śakti+pudgalaḥ is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: That soul is supreme; indeed, he is the haṃsa, the individual of power.

items.question: Where is the breath-filled vital air said to be situated in living beings?
premises: The vital air is filled with breath
This air is present in living beings
It is described as situated in all beings
items.inference: Therefore the breath-filled vital air abides in all living beings.
uncertainties: Agreement between vāyuḥ and saṃsthitam is irregular in the transmitted text.
items.plain_english: The breath-filled vital air is situated in all living beings.

items.question: What is the soul declared to be upon merely leaving the body?
premises: The soul leaves the body
This departure is described as mere leaving
At that point it is called supreme Śiva
items.inference: Therefore, upon leaving the body, the soul is declared to be supreme Śiva.
items.plain_english: As soon as he leaves the body, he is called the supreme Śiva.

items.question: How is this teaching transmitted and heard according to traditional succession?
premises: The teaching is heard in the ear
It comes down through succession
The goddess is addressed as recipient
items.inference: Therefore the teaching is received aurally through an unbroken traditional lineage.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, it is heard in the ear, having come down through the succession of tradition.

items.question: What effect arises from merely hearing this knowledge, O fair-faced one?
premises: The knowledge is merely heard
Hearing alone is emphasized
The fair-faced one is addressed
items.inference: Therefore even mere hearing of this knowledge is presented as efficacious.
uncertainties: The sentence is incomplete and continues in the next verse.
items.plain_english: O fair-faced one, by this mere knowledge, merely heard...

items.question: What disciplined practice over six months leads to a state free from bondage?
premises: Practice is prescribed for six months
The practitioner is described as one who practices
The goal is a state free from bondage
items.inference: Therefore one who practices for six months attains a state free from bondage.
uncertainties: The exact sense of kāṣāyaṃ here may be technical or metaphorical.
items.plain_english: But whoever practices for six months attains the ochre state, free from bondage.

items.question: What condition and companionship result from the prescribed spiritual practice?
premises: The practitioner becomes freed from all diseases
Association with yogis is mentioned
Union or meeting with them is attained
items.inference: Therefore the practice leads to freedom from disease and union with yogis.
uncertainties: The syntactic role of saha+melakam is compressed in the transmitted text.
items.plain_english: Freed from all diseases, he attains union together with the yogis.

items.question: What teaching has now been communicated to Bhairavī regarding the soul's practice?
premises: A teaching has been told
The teaching concerns the practice of the soul
Bhairavī is the addressed recipient
items.inference: Therefore the practice concerning the soul has now been explained to Bhairavī.
items.plain_english: O Bhairavī, this practice of the soul has been told to you.

rows.grounds: locative or dative sense; compound kṛta+niścaya

items.question: To what kind of resolved recipient may this teaching be given?
premises: The teaching is to be given
The recipient is endowed with all states
The recipient has a resolved mind
items.inference: Therefore the teaching may be given to a fully endowed person of firm resolve.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is endowed with all states and has a resolved mind.

items.question: Under what restriction must the Kaula essence originating from the yoginīs be withheld?
premises: The Kaula essence is mentioned
This essence originates from the yoginīs
It is explicitly declared not to be given
items.inference: Therefore the Kaula essence originating from the yoginīs must not be given indiscriminately.
items.plain_english: The Kaula essence, which has its origin in the yoginīs, must not be given.

rows.grounds: subject noun in accusative form in text

items.question: What transformation of the body is claimed after the veil of ignorance is struck away?
premises: The speaker refers to her body today
The body was struck by the veil of ignorance
The body is now described as pure
items.inference: Therefore the body is now experienced as pure, freed from the veil of ignorance.
uncertainties: The form deham is unexpected for the apparent subject role.
items.plain_english: Today my body is pure, having been struck free from the veil of ignorance.

items.question: What auspicious method for overcoming time does the speaker now wish to hear?
premises: The speaker expresses a present wish
The wish concerns hearing a teaching
The teaching concerns the auspicious overcoming of time
items.inference: Therefore the speaker now seeks instruction on the auspicious overcoming of time.
items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear the auspicious means of overcoming time.

items.question: What assurance is given about the destruction of death through the teaching?
premises: The speaker promises to explain
No doubt is asserted
Death is said to be destroyed
items.inference: Therefore the teaching is presented as a certain means by which death is destroyed.
items.plain_english: I shall tell you; there is no doubt, as to how death is destroyed.

items.question: How can even a wise person be affected while approaching the tip of nectar?
premises: The tip of nectar is mentioned
The essence of juice is involved
Even a wise person may be burning
items.inference: Therefore even the wise may experience burning in contact with the foremost nectar-essence.
uncertainties: The syntax and technical referents of amṛta+agraṃ and rasa+agreṇa are obscure.
items.plain_english: Even the wise one, burning with the foremost essence, at the tip of nectar...

items.question: What yogic action with the breath is prescribed at the root of tongue and palate?
premises: The locus is the root of tongue and palate
The breath is to be directed there
The breath should be drawn in slowly
items.inference: Therefore one should slowly draw in the breath at the root of the tongue and palate.
items.plain_english: Having placed it at the root of the tongue and palate, one should slowly drink in the breath.

rows.grounds: fused form with sandhi marker; relative time plus past participle

items.question: What result follows when this breath practice is maintained for one year?
premises: The practice is continued for one year
The practice becomes established
Old age and death are affected
items.inference: Therefore, when practiced for one year, old age and death are destroyed.
items.plain_english: When this has been practiced for one year, old age and death are destroyed.

rows.grounds: instrumental agent; compound mahā+uraga with internal sandhi

items.question: What immunity to poison is claimed for the practitioner bitten by great serpents?
premises: The practitioner may be bitten by great serpents
Poison is the expected danger
Poison does not enter the body
items.inference: Therefore the accomplished practitioner remains immune to poison even when bitten by great serpents.
items.plain_english: Even if bitten by great serpents, poison does not enter the body.
